slides.notes:
Welcome. Say: "Today: family." Point to the picture and say: "This is a family."
Say at the start: "You can talk about your family or Ana's family." Ana's family is the picture-card family. Every activity works with it.
Family can be a sensitive topic. Some learners have family far away or have lost family members. Never ask a learner to talk about their own family.
Class plan: 6:00 Hello + Review, 6:10 New Words, 6:20 Listening, 6:32 Grammar, 6:45 Break, 7:00 Talk Time, 7:10 Exit Ticket + Homework, 7:15 Letters & Numbers, 7:25 Progress Check.

slides.title: Who's this?

runs.t: Yes, I am.  /  No, I'm not.

slides.notes:
Box 2 is the key point. Ask: "Do you have kids?" Nod: "Yes, I do." Shake your head: "No, I don't."
Write on the board: Yes, I do. ✓ / Yes, I have. ✗. Then add the number: "Yes, I do. I have two."
Click to show each answer.
OPTIONAL: Are you married? Yes, I am. / No, I'm not. Learners don't have to answer. Do not ask this question to a learner in front of the class. Never ask "Where is your husband?" or "Why don't you have kids?"
Accept "No, I don't" and move on.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson4/Level1_Lesson4.md (Step 4: Grammar Box 2; Grammar page; Teacher notes).

slides.title: Who's this?

runs.t: This is my ___. Her name is ___.
Who's this? How old is he?

slides.notes:
Groups of 3. 15 learners: 5 groups. 7–8 learners: 2 groups of 3 + 1 pair (or 2 groups of 4).
Say again: "Your family or Ana's family. You choose." Don't ask who chooses what.
Model (2 min): fill in the board tree with your family or an invented family. Say 3 sentences: "This is my sister. Her name is Laura. She's 30." A learner asks you one question: "How old is he?"
Part 1 (3 min): each learner fills in the blank tree (names, ages if they want), or uses Ana's family. Learners who can't write yet can draw faces or point.
Part 2 (5 min): each person shows the tree and says 3 sentences (This is my ___. His / Her name is ___. He's / She's ___.). The others ask one question each (Who's this? How old is he? Do you have kids?).
Fast groups: one sentence with 's: "Rosa's son is 12." If behind: 2 sentences each, skip the questions.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson4/Level1_Lesson4.md (Step 5: Talk Time).

slides.title: Talk Time

runs.t: Yes, I do. / No, I don't.

slides.notes:
Exit ticket (never skip): each learner says one sentence about a family member (or a person in Ana's family): "This is my son. His name is…"
Or learners write "Yes, I do." / "No, I don't." for "Do you have kids?". Copying is fine.
Homework (10 minutes): open the Homework page. Do item 1 together (the first sentence). Point to each instruction.
Homework: 1) 3 sentences about your family or Ana's family; 2) do / don't; 3) 's (Carlos's son, Kim's brothers, Rosa's daughter); 4) ask a family member or a friend: Do you have kids? Do you have brothers or sisters?; 5) review: a phone number (a practice number is OK).
Homework answers: item 2: 1 do, 2 don't, 3 do, 4 don't.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson4/Level1_Lesson4.md (Step 6: Exit Ticket + Homework; Student Pages: Homework).

slides.title: Before You Go

slides.notes:
Letters & Numbers (10 min). Whole class, then pairs. Use the Letters & Numbers page, Task A.
See it (1 min): point to the 4 columns: a (dad), o (mom), u sound (son), i (kids). Click to show each row.
Say it (3 min): say each row. Learners repeat. The vowels are short: say them quickly.
son, mother, brother: the letter is o, but the sound is u (like but).
Quick check (1 min): say "dad" or "kids"… learners point to the row. Partners: A points to a word, B reads it. Switch.
Task C (one → two): brothers, sisters, sons, daughters, parents (child → children, no -s). Task D: copy "This is my mom." "This is my dad." Point to the capital T and the period.
Learners who can't read or write yet say the words with everyone and point. If behind: do Tasks A and B only.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson4/Level1_Lesson4.md (Letters & Numbers; Answer key, Task C).

slides.notes:
Task B. Say each word 2 times: 1 mom, 2 dad, 3 kids, 4 his, 5 big. Learners circle the word they hear.
Then click to show each answer circle. Pairs check.
Answer key: 1 mom, 2 dad, 3 kids, 4 his, 5 big.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson4/Level1_Lesson4.md (Answer key, Letters & Numbers Task B).
slides.title: Letters: Task B

runs.t: d. Yes, I do. I have two.

slides.notes:
Progress Check (5 min). Individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
Part A: read the 5 words slowly, 2 times each: 1 father, 2 daughter, 3 wife, 4 brother, 5 grandmother. Learners circle.
Parts B and C: learners match and write on their own. Help with the instructions only. Click to show the Part B answers when you check together: 1 c, 2 d, 3 a, 4 b.
Part C answers: 1 Her, 2 His, 3 Ana's.
Part D: read each "I can…" line and point to the 3 faces: 😀 "I can do it." 🙂 "A little." 😐 "Not yet." Learners check one.
Score: A /5 + B /4 + C /3 = /12. This is not a test grade. Collect the pages. If behind: do it in Week 5 at 6:00.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson4/Level1_Lesson4.md (Progress Check; Answer key).
